attribute.markdown:
**attribute** *nameClass* `{` *pattern* `}` — [Spec](https://relaxng.org/compact-tutorial-20030326.html#id2814218)

Defines an attribute pattern that matches an XML attribute. The *nameClass* specifies which attribute names match, and the *pattern* describes the allowed value.

By default, attributes are required. Use `?` to make them optional: `attribute id { text }?`.

**Examples:**
```rnc
attribute href { xsd:anyURI }
attribute type { "simple" | "complex" }
attribute id { text }?
```

text.markdown:
**text** — [Spec](https://relaxng.org/compact-tutorial-20030326.html#id2814100)

Matches any text content, including the empty string. When used inside an element pattern, it allows the element to contain arbitrary character data.

The `text` pattern is idempotent: `text, text` is equivalent to `text`.

**Examples:**
```rnc
element name { text }
element description { text }
```
text.plaintext:
text

Matches any text content, including the empty string.

See https://relaxng.org/compact-tutorial-20030326.html#id2814100

empty.markdown:
**empty** — [Spec](https://relaxng.org/compact-tutorial-20030326.html#id2819693)

Matches empty content: no text, no child elements. An element with the `empty` pattern may only contain attributes (if specified separately).

**Examples:**
```rnc
element br { empty }
element img { attribute src { xsd:anyURI }, empty }
```
empty.plaintext:
empty

Matches empty content: no text, no child elements.

See https://relaxng.org/compact-tutorial-20030326.html#id2819693

notAllowed.markdown:
**notAllowed** — [Spec](https://relaxng.org/compact-tutorial-20030326.html#id2819693)

A pattern that never matches. Used as the identity element for choice (`|`) — combining anything with `notAllowed` via choice yields the other pattern unchanged.

Commonly used for extensibility: a define starts as `notAllowed` and is extended via `|=` in including grammars.

**Examples:**
```rnc
extra.content = notAllowed
extra.content |= element note { text }
```
notAllowed.plaintext:
notAllowed

A pattern that never matches. Used for extensibility via combine operators.

See https://relaxng.org/compact-tutorial-20030326.html#id2819693

list.markdown:
**list** `{` *pattern* `}` — [Spec](https://relaxng.org/compact-tutorial-20030326.html#id2816748)

Matches a whitespace-separated list of tokens. The text content is split on whitespace, and each token must match the inner *pattern*.

**Examples:**
```rnc
attribute points { list { xsd:double+ } }
element classes { list { xsd:token+ } }
```

start.markdown:
**start** `=` *pattern* — [Spec](https://relaxng.org/compact-tutorial-20030326.html#id2814100)

Defines the start pattern of the grammar — the pattern that the root element must match.

Every grammar must have exactly one `start` declaration. Multiple `start` declarations can be combined using `|=` (choice) or `&=` (interleave).

**Examples:**
```rnc
start = element root { text }
start = myDefine
start |= element alternate { text }
```
start.plaintext:
start = pattern

Defines the start pattern of the grammar. The root element must match this pattern.

See https://relaxng.org/compact-tutorial-20030326.html#id2814100

include.markdown:
**include** *anyURILiteral* [ `{` *grammarContent* `}` ] — [Spec](https://relaxng.org/compact-tutorial-20030326.html#id2820475)

### `include` (reference)

Merges definitions from another RNC grammar file into the current grammar. The included defines become available as references.

```rnc
include "inline.rnc"

start = element doc {
  paragraph+
}
```

### `include { }` (override)

Includes a grammar file and overrides specific definitions. Definitions inside the body replace the corresponding definitions from the included file.

```rnc
include "inline.rnc" {
  paragraph = element p { text }
}
```

Only names that exist in the included file can be overridden — other names produce an error.

external.markdown:
**external** *anyURILiteral* [ *inherit* ] — [Spec](https://relaxng.org/compact-tutorial-20030326.html#id2820475)

References an external RELAX NG grammar and uses its start pattern as a sub-pattern. Unlike `include`, which merges definitions, `external` simply uses the other grammar's content.

**Examples:**
```rnc
start = external "other.rnc"
foo = element foo { external "bar-content.rnc" }
```

namespace.markdown:
**namespace** *prefix* `=` *anyURILiteral* — [Spec](https://relaxng.org/compact-tutorial-20030326.html#id2819036)

Declares a namespace prefix for use in element and attribute names. The prefix can then be used with a colon to qualify names: `prefix:localName`.

**Examples:**
```rnc
namespace a = "http://relaxng.org/ns/compatibility/annotations/1.0"
namespace html = "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml"
start = element html:html { text }
```

Declares a namespace prefix for use in qualified element and attribute names.

See https://relaxng.org/compact-tutorial-20030326.html#id2819036

default.markdown:
**default namespace** [ *prefix* ] `=` *anyURILiteral* — [Spec](https://relaxng.org/compact-tutorial-20030326.html#id2819036)

Declares the default namespace for unqualified element names. Optionally assigns a prefix that can also be used to explicitly qualify names.

**Examples:**
```rnc
default namespace = "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml"
default namespace html = "http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml"
```
default.plaintext:
default namespace [ prefix ] = anyURILiteral

Declares the default namespace for unqualified element names.

See https://relaxng.org/compact-tutorial-20030326.html#id2819036

datatypes.markdown:
**datatypes** *prefix* `=` *anyURILiteral* — [Spec](https://relaxng.org/compact-tutorial-20030326.html#id2817679)

Declares a datatypes library prefix. The most common datatype library is XML Schema datatypes (`xsd`), which provides types like `xsd:string`, `xsd:integer`, `xsd:anyURI`, etc.

**Examples:**
```rnc
datatypes xsd = "http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-datatypes"
attribute age { xsd:positiveInteger }
```

See https://relaxng.org/compact-tutorial-20030326.html#id2817679

inherit.markdown:
**inherit** — [Spec](https://relaxng.org/compact-tutorial-20030326.html#id2819036)

Used in namespace declarations to inherit the default namespace from the including grammar.

**Examples:**
```rnc
namespace local = inherit
include "other.rnc" inherit
```

inherit

See https://relaxng.org/compact-tutorial-20030326.html#id2819036

string.markdown:
**string** [ *params* ] — [Spec](https://relaxng.org/compact-tutorial-20030326.html#id2817679)

Built-in datatype that matches a string value with whitespace preserved. This is the default datatype when no library is specified.

**Examples:**
```rnc
attribute type { string "fixed" }
element value { string }
```

token.markdown:
**token** [ *params* ] — [Spec](https://relaxng.org/compact-tutorial-20030326.html#id2817679)

Built-in datatype that matches a tokenized string: leading and trailing whitespace is stripped, and internal whitespace is collapsed to single spaces before comparison.

**Examples:**
```rnc
attribute class { token "main" }
element name { token }
```

Built-in datatype that matches a tokenized string (whitespace collapsed).

See https://relaxng.org/compact-tutorial-20030326.html#id2817679
